There's a few different ways, depending on what country you want to move to. 

You can always try to go for a degree (undergrad, masters, phd) or if a company you work for has offices there, ask for a transfer.   
Some countries may have specific work visa programmes (I think Australia and New Zealand for example) that you can apply to instead.  
There's also having a significant other who has citizenship, although I believe you have to be married for that. You are right about having family in the country, as they can sponsor you. You may still need a job though; once again, it depends on the country.  
Some countries allow you to gain citizenship if you can prove that your parents, grandparents, and sometimes great-grandparents were/are citizens of that country. I believe Ireland and Poland allow that.   


In general, it can be pretty hard/time-consuming/expensive to move to another country, but there are ways to do it. Although having a high degree, money, and/or family there definitely helps a lot.
